doc: Held-Hou raw Hadley edge (degrees, NOT clamped, inf for no spin) of the named bodies (Earth, Mars, Titan, Venus, a 0.4-day fast rotator, a retrograde Earth, a 4-day slow rotator, a 2-radius super-Earth, a small moon, five bodies at the 50 degree eddy threshold) and degenerate rows (no spin as None/NaN/inf/-inf/0/-0, subnormal and huge periods, zero, negative, NaN and infinite gravity, scale height and radius, odd regime strings). Float64 closed form (sqrt, a few products): rtol 1e-9, a 1-ulp nudge of every input of the regular rows moves the result by under 2e-15 relative (a nudge of a degenerate row can cross its branch). inf is compared as inf. Python details a port must copy: gravity * scale height goes through max(0.0, g H), which returns 0.0 for a NaN product (Rust f64::max ignores a NaN operand too; clamp does not); a non-finite or zero period (None, NaN, +-inf, +-0) gives inf; a NaN radius gives NaN. NaN and infinities may appear in the inputs (a rotation period None is stored as NaN) and in the outputs: NaN equals NaN, an infinity equals the same infinity (sign included).

params.note: a NaN rotation period stands for None or NaN: both mean no spin
